# JOURNAL — optimizer handover (append-only, whole run)

YOU (the optimizer) own this file. It is the running, accumulating handover across ALL iterations — accepted AND rejected — and it is NEVER reset. Each iteration you APPEND one new entry at the bottom (under the marker line); you do NOT edit or delete earlier entries. Read the whole journal before proposing, so you build on EVERY prior attempt (not just the last accepted one) and never re-test a refuted idea.

You CANNOT know your own gate result while you write — the harness scores you AFTER you stop and stamps a **RESULT** line (outcome + Δ + the tasks you measurably broke/fixed, plus the ones whose move was too small to resolve) right below your entry. So do NOT write 'what worked' as a guess. To learn what actually worked, READ the framework RESULT lines of prior entries (and LEDGER.md): an entry whose RESULT says `rejected` with `broke={...}` tells you which specific edits to drop or redesign — its diff.patch is in ./prior_iterations/<id>/.

Append your entry for THIS iteration below the marker, using this shape (INTENT only — the framework appends the RESULT):

    ## Iteration <your candidate id> — <one-line headline of what you tried>
    - Changes I made (1 line per edit; name the file/tool + cluster it targets):
    - Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe (which failing task it should fix;
      why no passing task changes behavior):
    - Building on prior RESULTS: which prior entries' broke/fixed I used, and what I
      did NOT re-try because a prior RESULT showed it regressed (cite ids):
    - Refuted hypotheses (a prior RESULT proved this is NOT the fix — never re-test):
    - High-value clusters still NOT cracked (and the guard/tool designs already tried):
    - Plateau signal (are the last few RESULTs flat/negative? if so, which LEVER to switch
      to — e.g. a NEW composite tool instead of another guard, or prompt instead of code):
    - Cost-reduction opportunity (if `cost`/`latency`/`num_messages` is a declared objective,
      run `detect_loop_patterns.py --run-dir $R --tag $BEST --split val` — free, no extra
      eval — and check its `by_tool` map for a same-tool-called-N-times-in-a-row pattern. A
      hit names the exact tool + repeat count: propose a composite/bulk tool (capability
      `tools`), a bundled script entrypoint (`skills-package`), or upfront-batched
      instructions (`prompt`/`system-prompt`) that replace the N calls with one. No hit
      (or cost/latency not a declared objective): say so plainly, do not leave this blank):
    - Focus next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 — Verified that 53/67 tasks bypass orchestrator.md; spent the budget on shared_context.md + domain files, and deleted three FALSE baseline rules that were themselves causing failures

- **Changes I made** (1 line per edit; file + cluster):
  - `aap2_agent.md`/`babylon_agent.md`: **deleted** "Always use `get_job_log` instead of `get_job`" (×2) and corrected "fetch_github_file — Fetch files and directories" + the Splunk "controller hostname / `cluster_host_id`" instruction. These three baseline sentences were the *cause* of clusters on platform-126/116, platform-121/007/137, platform-112/155.
  - `shared_context.md`: result-scope discipline (scope label / clamped period / placeholder zeros / absent field / staleness; failed input ≠ zero; don't combine mismatched extents; a numeric filter drops rows lacking the field; an empty result is only evidence about the scope you chose) → cost-407/408/418/402/051.
  - `shared_context.md`: do-the-feasible-reads-then-decline + never repair a malformed identifier → cloud-057/058 (both made ZERO tool calls in 8/10 and 10/10 trials).
  - `shared_context.md`: repo file fetching by path shape + `/runner/project/` log paths + pin the known ref + bounded stop-and-answer → platform-121/032/007/137.
  - `shared_context.md`: answer-surface contract (one plain sentence per question; state word right after the name, no icon between; finding-shaped headings; bare-digit non-currency counts; margins from raw values) → icinga-045/204/201, platform-116/101/153.
  - `shared_context.md`: lifecycle cost-series split (exact daily sums, boundary rule) + unconditional go/no-go verdict → cost-419/410. Line-citation-by-number rule → platform-152/153/136/101.
  - `icinga_agent.md`: epoch→UTC month-anchor table + div/mod arithmetic + worked example (**placed here, not in the shared file**, after confirming no non-icinga task has epochs in tool results) → icinga-215/204/206/216/212. Plus `command_endpoint`/`check_source` follow-through → icinga-222.
  - `cost_agent.md`: aggregate-label rows (read the entity from the row's item KEY first), preset placeholder zeros, clamped `period`, GCP figures net of credits → cost-407/402/418/051.
  - `security_agent.md`: `userIdentity.username` (lowercase) + null fallback → cloud-057/317; in-force decided by `agreement_end`+`auto_renew` not `status`, citing `last_updated` → stale-status class; region from the provisioning record, empty region ≠ nothing launched → platform-158.
  - `orchestrator.md`: deliberately MINIMAL (+27 lines) — route by data source not topic words, resolve an identifier in its own domain first and pass values on, finish a step a sub-agent could not run.
- **Expected effect + why it's safe:** per-edit verify-the-fix and the protects-passing column are in PROCESS.md. The highest-confidence items are the three false-rule corrections (each maps to a 9–10/10-trial unmatched expected call) and the epoch table (I recomputed all 36 anchors; the target conversions land exactly on the graded values). Every rule is phrased over tool-result structure or answer form, never over task content; a grep audit for task literals is clean.
- **Building on prior RESULTS:** none exist — this is iteration 1 of the run. `LEDGER.md`, `RUNMAP.md`, `INSIGHTS.md` and `rejected.jsonl` were all empty, so there was nothing to avoid re-testing and no prior diff to extend.
- **Refuted hypotheses:** none confirmed by a RESULT yet. But my OWN first draft was falsified before shipping by two review subagents (one of which executed target tasks' `verify.py`): a broad "two empty calls → stop" rule would have cut passing platform-062 short in 4/10 trials; "name who can do it" tripped platform-118's forbidden `recreate`; "never combine figures whose scopes differ" forbade platform-041's graded difference; a generic exclusive-end-date aside endangered platform-018's pinned `created_before`; my staleness rule made *every* `last_check` stale; and my `org-wide` rule was factually wrong for cost-073's linked-account grouping. All six were fixed with named carve-outs — **do not re-broaden them.** I also had to replace every example value in my first draft, because they had been lifted from graded answers (the epoch example was its own task's expected timestamp).
- **High-value clusters still NOT cracked:** the **routing fast-path** (~3.4 task-points — the largest in the run, bigger than everything I fixed). `classify_fast()` dispatches 53/67 tasks to a sub-agent chosen by regex on topic words, and that agent often has no tool for the task's data source and cannot hand off (cloud-304/315 → cost without `query_marketplace_agreements`; icinga-013/platform-071 → babylon without `query_icinga`; cloud-074/310 → babylon without `query_aws_costs`; cost-410/419 → cost without `query_aap2`). **No prompt edit can reach these** — verified by reading both call sites. Needs a code fix; escalated in FRAMEWORK_IMPROVEMENTS.md. Designs already tried: none, because the edit space excludes it.
- **Plateau signal:** n/a, first iteration. The lever I chose deliberately: *correct/delete harmful existing text* over *append new preamble*, after finding three baseline sentences were causal. If this is rejected with no clear per-task cause, the first hypothesis should be **attention dilution** — `shared_context.md` went 237→491 lines and is prepended to every sub-agent; split the remaining rules into domain files rather than rewriting them.
- **Cost-reduction opportunity:** `cost`/`latency`/`num_messages` are **not** declared objectives for this run (the only declared focus is val reward), so I did not run `detect_loop_patterns.py`. Stating that plainly rather than leaving it blank. Incidentally, two edits should *reduce* calls anyway: the directory-fetch correction removes a 3–5-call thrash loop on several github tasks, and the bounded stop rule ends trajectories that currently exhaust their rounds.
- **Focus next iteration:** (1) If accepted — re-measure and attack the answer-surface and line-citation clusters, which I expect to be the flakiest of my edits. (2) If rejected — test the dilution hypothesis by splitting `shared_context.md`'s additions into the domain files that need them, keeping only the genuinely domain-general rules shared. (3) Either way, the fast-path cluster is worth more than anything left in the prompt space; if the framework can enable a code or routing fix, do that before more prose.
